headline: The 'Is Cereal a Soup?' Debate Has Somehow Gotten Worse
subheadline: New faction argues soup is a cereal; original camps united in opposition
summary: The classic internet debate about cereal's categorical status has escalated with a provocative new position.
content:
The long-running internet debate over whether cereal qualifies as soup has escalated dramatically with the emergence of a third faction arguing that, actually, soup is a type of cereal.

The original debate, which has persisted online since at least 2015, traditionally featured two camps: those who argue cereal is soup (a liquid base with solid components served in a bowl) and those who insist it isn't (soup is hot, soup is savory, soup has different cultural contexts).

But a new position has emerged that has united the former opponents. User u/ReverseDiet posted: "You're both wrong. Soup is a cereal. Think about it. Cereal came first. Grains in liquid. Soup is just hot cereal with vegetables. Soup is derived from cereal. Soup is a subcategory of cereal."

The post has achieved something unprecedented: the "cereal is soup" and "cereal is not soup" factions have temporarily allied against the common enemy.

"I have fought the 'cereal is soup' people for years," wrote one traditionalist. "But I would rather lose to them honorably than see this 'soup is cereal' nonsense gain traction. There are limits."

The new position has 847 dedicated supporters who call themselves "Cerealians" and have developed an elaborate taxonomy placing all foods on a cereal-to-not-cereal spectrum. Under their system, soup scores 0.7 cereal, stew scores 0.5 cereal, and solid foods like steak score 0.0 cereal.

"It's a unified theory of food," explained u/ReverseDiet. "Once you accept that cereal is the base state of cuisine—grain and liquid—everything else is just variation."

Food scientists have declined to engage with the debate, with one stating: "I went to school for eight years. I'm not answering questions about whether soup is breakfast."

At press time, a fourth faction arguing that "all food is just rearranged soup" had begun organizing.
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
